 Paris R2 previews and predictions: Jodar vs. Ruud, Shelton vs. Norrie 
 November 2, 2026 
 Cheryl Murray 
 Match previews 
 12 
 Andrew Patron/Delray Beach Open 
 The Paris Masters delivers two tasty second-round matches on Tuesday, as record-breaking Rafael Jodar takes on Casper Ruud and Nitto ATP Finals-bound Ben Shelton battles veteran lefty Cam Norrie. 
 (10) Rafael Jodar vs. Casper Ruud 
 Rafael Jodar is now the first ATP player to break into the top 10 in his debut season on tour. He is also trying to be the first player to qualify for the NextGen ATP Finals and the Nitto ATP Finals in the same year. The Spaniard sits ninth in the live race to Turin — a qualifying position since No. 2 Jannik Sinner is out with an injury. Casper Ruud got past qualifier Juan Manuel Cerundolo 6-3, 6-2 on Monday, but the Norwegian is unseeded and the Rolex Paris Masters has not been kind to him, either. He lost his opening match to Francisco Cerundolo in 2024 and to Daniel Altmaier last year.
 These two met just a few weeks ago in Shanghai, where Ruud took the first set before Jodar turned it around 4-6, 6-4, 6-3 behind 28 winners and some lethal counterpunching. Surprisingly, Ruud is solid indoor player with a 55-33 career record — but he is unlucky to run into a motivated Jodar, who will be trying to lock up his spot in Turin.
 Cheryl pick: Jodar in 2 
 Ricky pick: Jodar in 2

 (3) Ben Shelton vs. Cam Norrie 
 Ben Shelton has made headlines this week by announcing a coaching arrangement with former Carlos Alcaraz team member Juan Carlos Ferrero. The news comes following weeks of speculation regarding which top player Ferrero signed up with following his split from Alcaraz.
Shelton opens his Paris campaign as the third seed, a career-high world No. 4, and he is already booked for Turin. However, the fall swing has been rough. Since losing the U.S. Open final to Alexander Zverev, the American has won just two of six matches. He dropped both Davis Cup singles rubbers against Czechia, lost to Arthur Gea in the third round of Shanghai, and went out to world No. 222 Jerome Kym in a third-set tiebreaker in Basel. Cameron Norrie delivered a huge upset on this court last year when he shocked Alcaraz. The Brit has endured a disappointing fall, though, and arrived in Paris with no momentum. Norrie won their only previous meeting, a 6-0, 6-2 drubbing in Cincinnati back in 2022 — when Shelton was still a Florida Gator trying to decide whether to go pro. Suffice it to say he is no longer the same player.
 Cheryl pick: Shelton in 2 
 Ricky pick: Shelton in 3
